![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068149/assets/d8be54eddd0358742170a03b3c55e0cb94eaf2a7d59f12e1c4361a6197d29847.png)
Consider the initial value problem and its solution given above. What is the tangent vector to the solution curve at the point corresponding to $t=\ln 2?$
e-21585.worked_solution:
Recall that the $xy$-coordinate plane is called the *phase plane* of the system. A particular solution of an initial value problem is called a *trajectory* (or *orbit*).

First, we compute the point that corresponds to $t=\ln 2$ on the given trajectory:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & ={e}^{3(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =8[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+2\cdot 2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =8[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the equation of our system, we obtain the tangent vector to the trajectory.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2(12)+1(4) \\ 1(12)+2(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24+4 \\ 12+8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}28 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t)-2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-4x(t)+y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above and its trajectory passing through the point $(0,-2)$ in the phase space of the system. What is the tangent vector to the trajectory at this point?
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the $xy$-coordinate plane is called the *phase plane* of the system. A particular solution of an initial value problem is called a *trajectory* (or *orbit*).

In our case, the trajectory (solution) passes through the point $(x,y)=(0,-2)$ in the phase space. Substituting the coordinates of this point into the equations of our system, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} & =3x-2y \\  & =3(0)-2(-2) \\  & =0+4 \\  & =4 \\ {y}^{′} & =-4x+y \\  & =-4(0)+(-2) \\  & =0-2 \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent vector to the trajectory is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} \\ {y}^{′}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
